Subject: Post-call recap: Acme POC goals & next steps

Hi Lara / Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time earlier — great conversation. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps for the POC/trial: 

Summary of goals
- Validate Redwood inference quality for Acme’s customer support summarization pipeline for 5k daily sessions
- Verify end-to-end latency under 150ms p50 for single-request generation with streaming enabled
- Confirm integration pattern (server-to-server API + prefix caching) and ease of model swapping

Success criteria (proposed)
1) Accuracy: average ROUGE-L and human spot-checks show summaries meet your internal bar (we can adopt your rubric)
2) Latency: p50 < 150ms, p95 < 400ms for 99% of test traffic
3) Stability: no more than one service interruption >5 minutes during the 2-week trial
4) Integration: SDK-based integration with streaming and tool-calling proof-of-concept working in your staging environment

POC plan & timeline (target)
- Week 0 (this week): share success criteria doc + integration checklist (attached)
- Week 1: Redwood provides SDK snippets + sandbox API keys; your engineers begin integration (streaming + tool calling)
- Week 2: Run synthetic load and sample production traffic for metrics; joint quality review; adjust prompts/temperature
- Week 3: Final evaluation and go/no-go decision; optional extension for further tuning

Ownership
- Redwood: Marissa (program/engaging), Dylan (solutions engineer) for technical onboarding and runbook
- Acme: Lara (product), Tom (engineering lead), Acme IT for network/firewall setup

Next steps (action items)
- Marissa: send success criteria doc and integration checklist (attached) — COMPLETED
- Acme: confirm availability for a 30-min kick-off with engineering (propose Wed 8/12 or Thu 8/13)
- Dylan/Vivek: prepare SDK examples for node/python + streaming demo

Attachments: acme_poc_success_criteria.docx, redwood_integration_checklist.xlsx

If that aligns, I’ll schedule the kickoff.

Cheers,
Marissa

Hi all — adding the technical alignment items we discussed. Pasting a short checklist and a minimal Node + Python streaming snippet. Happy to demo on the kickoff.

Technical checklist (integration/implementation)
- SDKs: node (recommended for your app stack) and python examples included
- Auth: sandbox API key + recommended short-lived token pattern for server-to-server calls
- API routes: POST /v1/generate for non-streamed; POST /v1/stream for chunked token streaming (server-sent events/HTTP2); WebSocket is also available if you prefer
- Prefix caching: use our SDK caching helper to store KV-cache between requests for repeated sessions
- Tool calling pattern: Model emits a tool call event with metadata; Redwood runtime will call your endpoint (signed webhook). If you need the outbound call to go through your VPC connector, we support configuring an HTTPS callback to your staging host.
- Observability: include x-request-id header; we’ll provide per-token cost/latency breakdowns in the Console for the POC
- Load testing: recommendations in the checklist — ramp to 5 RPS initially, then to 50 RPS synthetic for p95 characterization

Minimal Node streaming example (sketch):
- const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY })
- const stream = client.stream('/v1/stream', { model: 'redwood-1-small', prompt })
- stream.on('token', (t) => process.stdout.write(t))
- stream.on('tool_call', (tool) => { /* make outbound call to filter endpoint; return result */ })

Security/network notes
- If Acme requires egress restriction, we can coordinate with your infra to set up a private connector and provide static egress IPs for the POC.
- We sign outbound webhooks with HMAC header; shared secret exchange is supported.

I’ll attach the snippets and a short swagger of the callback contract after this message.

— Dylan
